core.title: Keep each product capability at least as cohesive internally as coupled to any single neighbor product capability (advisory)
core.given: A product capability (at or above the min-graph-size guard) whose DESIRED OUTCOMES, connected when they share >= min_shared salient object_of_control tokens, form one undirected graph with neighboring product capabilities' DESIRED OUTCOMES
core.when: You author or revise the product capability's DESIRED OUTCOMES, allocate DESIRED OUTCOMES across product capabilities, or review existing product capabilities
core.then: Plan the product capability so its cohesion (intra-wagon DESIRED OUTCOME edges) is >= its coupling (cross-wagon edges) to every single neighbor product capability; otherwise expect an advisory merge-suggestion signal.
prefer: When a product capability is more bound to one neighbor than to itself, treat the advisory merge-suggestion signal as a hint to consider merging it with that neighbor.
Judge cohesion and coupling on the same DESIRED OUTCOME shared-token graph so the two counts are commensurable.
avoid: Treating the merge-suggestion finding as blocking or gating the plan — it is advisory only and never blocks.
Flagging product capabilities below the min-graph-size guard on account of separability.
Rewording object_of_control tokens merely to dodge shared-token edges instead of reconsidering the product capability boundary.
unless: The product capability is below the configured min-graph-size guard: it is skipped, not flagged.
core.why: A product capability should be a separable unit of work; if it is more bound to one neighbor than to itself, its boundary may be wrong, so the advisory signal suggests considering a merge with its tightest neighbor.
evidence: The product capability separability check's output shows no merge-suggestion advisory for the product capability, or the product capability is reported as skipped by the min-graph-size guard.
For a flagged product capability: cohesion(W) and max over neighbors N of coupling(W,N) counts from the single DESIRED OUTCOME shared-token graph.
verification: Build one undirected graph over all DESIRED OUTCOMES; an edge joins two DESIRED OUTCOMES that share >= the configured min_shared of salient tokens taken from object_of_control.
cohesion(W) = number of intra-wagon edges; coupling(W,N) = number of cross-wagon edges between W and neighbor N.

Separable iff cohesion(W) >= max over neighbors N of coupling(W,N); non-separable product capabilities emit an ADVISORY merge-suggestion finding (the exact finding label and the emitting validator are realization details of this rule).
Cohesion and coupling must be measured on the same DESIRED OUTCOME shared-token graph (commensurable).
Product capabilities below the min-graph-size guard are skipped, not flagged.
Token vocabulary, min_shared and the min-graph-size guard are config-driven calibration knobs owned by the realization's configuration; promotion to a strict disposition is deferred to calibration.
Disposition advisory, severity 2: the finding never blocks.

values: merge-suggestion advisory emitted by the product capability separability assessment

fires: A product capability meeting the min-graph-size guard has, on the single DESIRED OUTCOME shared-token graph (edges = DESIRED OUTCOME pairs sharing >= min_shared salient object_of_control tokens), fewer intra-wagon edges than the qualifying cross-wagon edges to some single neighbor product capability.
A corpus-wide separability assessment of existing product capabilities (no edit in progress) finds such a product capability and emits an advisory merge-suggestion finding.
doesNotFire: A product capability with fewer DESIRED OUTCOMES than the configured min-graph-size guard (skipped, not flagged).
A product capability whose intra-wagon edge count is greater than or equal to its cross-wagon edge count with every single neighbor product capability (equality is separable).
Edits to code or tests that do not change product capabilities, DESIRED OUTCOMES or their object_of_control.

neutralityNotes: The convention is essentially stack-neutral: it operates entirely on the ATDD plan corpus (product capabilities, DESIRED OUTCOMES, object_of_control tokens), which is method vocabulary shared across stacks and already reflected in the profile vocabulary (layout.capability_dir, layout.plan_item, urn.desired-outcome), so the core keeps those terms. Three realization-specific tokens could not be neutralized and are carried in bunOnly: the '[MERGE]' finding label and the exact finding id '[MERGE] product capability separability', the 'separability validator' naming, and the 'planner.capability.*' configuration namespace for the calibration knobs. The knob values themselves (token vocabulary, min_shared, min-graph-size) are deliberately left unnamed numbers in the core: they are config-driven calibration owned by each realization's configuration, and promotion to a strict disposition is deferred to calibration, exactly as in the Bun text. The only profile dependency is which concrete artifact kinds play the capability-manifest and desired-outcome-definition roles (roles.plan_artifact.kinds); no vocabulary key was missing, so proposedKeys is empty.
